dhp129:1: Everyone trembles at the stick, everyone is in fear of death,
dhp129:3: comparing oneself (with others), one should not hurt or have (them) hurt.
dhp130:1: Everyone trembles at the stick, for all of them life is dear,
dhp130:3: comparing oneself (with others), one should not hurt or have (them) hurt.
dhp131:1: One who harms with a stick beings who desire happiness,
dhp131:4: while seeking happiness for himself, won’t find happiness after death.
dhp132:1: One who harms not with a stick beings who desire happiness,
dhp132:4: while seeking happiness for himself, will find happiness after death.
dhp133:1: Do not say anything harsh, spoken to they might answer back to you,
dhp133:3: for arrogant talk entails misery, and they might strike you back with a stick.
dhp134:2: If you make no sound like a gong that is broken,
dhp134:4: you are (like) one who has attained Nibbāna, contention is not found in you.
dhp135:1: Like a cowherd with a stick drives cattle to pasture,
dhp135:3: so do old age and death drive life out of beings.
dhp136:2: The fool does not understand the wicked deeds he is doing,
dhp136:3: the stupid one is consumed by his deeds as (by) a burning fire.
dhp137:2: Whoever offends with a stick those who are inoffensive and harmless
dhp137:3: will quickly fall into one of ten states:
dhp138:1: harsh feelings, loss (of his wealth), and the break up of the body,
dhp138:4: or even heavy affliction, or surely he will lose his mind,
dhp139:2: (there may be) danger from the King, or slander that is terrible,
dhp139:4: (he may suffer from) loss of kin, or (from) the destruction of wealth,
dhp140:1: also his houses may be consumed by flames and fire,
dhp140:3: and at the break-up of the body that one lacking in wisdom will arise in the underworld.
dhp141:1: Not going naked, nor matted hair, nor mud,
dhp141:2: nor fasting or lying on stony ground,
dhp141:3: dust and dirt, (or) striving while squatting,
dhp141:4: can purify a mortal who has not removed uncertainty.
dhp142:1: Even if he were to adorn himself,
dhp142:3: and has put aside the stick towards all beings,
dhp142:4: he is a brahmin, an ascetic, a monastic.
dhp143:2: Whatever person in the world is found restrained by conscience,
dhp143:4: and is aware of his fault, is like a good horse that is (restrained) by a whip.
dhp144:1: Like a good horse restrained by the whip,
dhp144:2: you should be ardent and spiritually intense.
dhp144:4: concentration and investigation of the Dhamma.
dhp144:5: One who has understanding and good conduct, mindfulness,
dhp144:6: will abandon this not insignificant suffering.
dhp145:5: The Chapter about the Stick, the Tenth
